newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end easier, Olivetti suspended.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end easier, Olivetti suspended.

text.p: Italian shares closed easier in a sober mood on Thursday with Olivetti shares suspended, but stocks moved off the early day's lows helped by a rally in bonds and the lira, dealers said.
Stocks had opened around one percent lower with little trading interest being seen while a lower Wall Street opening this afternoon kept buyers on the defensive.
Focus was again on Olivetti shares suspended by watchdog Consob ahead of meeting with its top management and former Olivetti director general who did not agree with results.
The all-share Mibtel index ended off 0.58 percent at 9,284 and the blue-chip Mib30 index off 0.68 percent at 13,767.

The Consob meeting aims to get further information after Renzo Francesconi, Olivetti's director general, resigned Wednesday saying he did not agree with group half-year results released on Tuesday. Olivetti chief executive Francesco Caio expected to attend meeting, but says results were true.
Olivetti shares were suspended at yesterday's closing price of 749 lire.

Investors largely ignored mutual funds data, which showed the inflow for August fell to 4.7 trillion lire from 6.9 trillion lire in July, and also offical August CPI annual inflation of 3.4 percent after July's 3.6 percent.
"It has been another dull day, with only the rally in bonds and the lira giving any support," said one trader.
STET was one share to shine, up 1.15 percent to 4,755 lire, after IRI approved the spinning off of STET's yellow pages publishing subsidiary Seat.
Most others were lower with Fiat off 0.43 percent to 4,445, Montedison down 0.39 percent at 941.3 lire, while De Benedetti family group CIR was 6.93 percent lower at 695.2 lire.
